claim: SWE-agent is the Princeton/Stanford research agent that gives a language model a custom agent-computer interface to autonomously resolve GitHub issues; it is the canonical academic reference implementation.

claim: OpenHands (formerly OpenDevin) is a production-oriented AI-driven development platform offering bash, file editing, browser and Jupyter tools, with an SDK, CLI, local GUI and cloud deployment.
quote: OpenHands: AI-Driven Development

claim: Aider is a terminal-native, git-first pair-programming agent that produces diff-based edits and commits each AI change as a git commit for review.
quote: Aider is AI pair programming in your terminal

claim: Cline is an open-source autonomous coding agent living in the IDE that plans multi-step changes, edits files, runs commands and the browser while requiring explicit human approval and showing diff previews at each step.
quote: Cline - AI Coding, Open Source and Uncompromised

claim: gptme is a provider-agnostic terminal AI agent equipped with shell, Python, web and vision tools, runnable on laptops, SSH sessions, headless servers and CI pipelines.
quote: Your agent in your terminal, equipped with local tools: writes code, uses the terminal, browses the web.

claim: gpt-engineer is a CLI codegen platform that generates whole projects from natural-language specs and iterates on improvements; it is an early-generation write-code agent and precursor to Lovable.
quote: CLI platform to experiment with codegen. Precursor to: https://lovable.dev

claim: Devika is the first open-source agentic software engineer, started as an open-source alternative to Devin, supporting Claude 3, GPT-4, Gemini, Mistral, Groq and local Ollama models; the project is now largely dormant.
quote: Devika is the first open-source implementation of an Agentic Software Engineer. Initially started as an open-source alternative to Devin.

claim: OpenHands ships a dedicated PR Review workflow triggered by a 'review-this' label or by requesting openhands-agent as a reviewer; it posts feedback in 2-3 minutes covering code quality, security concerns, and best practices, with custom skill files for project conventions.
quote: Triggers ... Adding the review-this label ... Requesting openhands-agent as a reviewer ... The review examines code through three primary lenses: Code Quality ... Security Concerns ... Best Practices

claim: The OpenHands GitHub Resolver runs as a GitHub Action that auto-fixes issues tagged with a label and opens a pull request in minutes, putting an open-source coding agent directly in the GitHub workflow.
quote: uses AI to automatically fix github issues and send pull requests ... fix any issues in your repository that you tag with the fix-me label

claim: Aider's architect mode lets a planning model discuss design and structure before a separate editor model applies edits, and the /diff command plus auto-commits make every change reviewable; a dedicated review mode remains only an open feature request.
quote: architect mode ... helps you plan things out ... The editor model uses one of aider's edit formats ... aider edits a file, it commits those changes with a descriptive commit message

claim: Aider maintains the Polyglot Leaderboard (launched Dec 2024, tracking 25+ models across Go, Rust, Java, JavaScript and C++), positioned as a multi-language counterweight to SWE-bench which is 100% Python with Django nearly half its cases.
quote: The Aider Polyglot Leaderboard, launched in December 2024 and now tracking over 25 models ... in contrast to SWE-bench which is 100% Python, with Django alone comprising nearly half of all its test cases

claim: On SWE-bench Verified, frontier scores reached the high 80s in 2026 (GPT-5.5 ~88.7% in May 2026), but the SWE-agent v1 open scaffold on Claude Sonnet 4.5 scores ~43.2%, showing scaffold choice and model both matter.
quote: SWE-agent v1 on Claude Sonnet 4.5 scores 43.2% on Verified ... GPT-5.5 leads SWE-Bench Verified at 88.7% as of May 2026

claim: LangGraph is favored for code-review bots, e.g. a security agent -> performance agent -> report agent pipeline, because it offers an explicit state graph with checkpointing, streaming and human-in-the-loop primitives.
quote: LangGraph shines for code review bots... security agent -> performance agent -> report agent workflow... LangGraph gives you an explicit state graph with checkpointing, streaming, and human-in-the-loop primitives

claim: In Alice Labs' 2026 production-tested ranking LangGraph is #1 for production (graph-based orchestration), Claude Agent SDK #2 (powers Claude Code), CrewAI #3 for fast multi-agent prototypes, and AutoGen/AG2 #4 for research-style agent conversations, with Pydantic AI a credible alternative gaining meaningful adoption through 2025.
quote: LangGraph leads as '#1 for production'... Claude Agent SDK ranks second... CrewAI places third... AutoGen/AG2 ranks fourth for 'research-style agent conversations'... 'Pydantic AI emerged as a credible alternative'

claim: The original Microsoft AutoGen repository remains the most-starred of the agentic frameworks but has been placed in maintenance mode with development moving to Microsoft Agent Framework.
quote: A programming framework for agentic AI

claim: Microsoft merged AutoGen's multi-agent orchestration with Semantic Kernel's enterprise foundations into the unified Microsoft Agent Framework (public preview Oct 1 2025); both predecessors entered maintenance mode and Agent Framework targets 1.0 GA by end of Q1 2026.

claim: Microsoft Agent Framework, the production-ready successor converging AutoGen and Semantic Kernel, has reached ~11k GitHub stars.

claim: Pydantic AI brings type-safe schema-defined agents with built-in OpenTelemetry instrumentation and agent-delegation (one agent calling another as a tool), making it a credible code-review-pipeline option, at ~17.6k stars.

claim: Pydantic AI treats an agent as a high-level construct defined by data schemas and Python functions and supports agent delegation where one agent invokes another as a tool, while LangGraph models agents as a graph of states and transitions suited to multi-stage diff analysis.
quote: Pydantic AI treats an agent as a high-level construct defined by data schemas and Python functions, whereas LangGraph treats an agent as a graph of states and transitions

claim: SWE-bench evaluates whether language models can resolve real-world GitHub issues by generating a patch that passes the repository's tests; it is an issue-resolution (bug-fix) benchmark, not a review-comment-quality benchmark.
quote: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-world Github Issues?

claim: On the SWE-bench Verified leaderboard in 2026, top frontier models report resolution rates around 82-88%, with leading entries such as GPT-5.5 (~82.6%) and Claude Opus 4.7/4.8 (~82-88%).
quote: GPT 5.5 leads with a performance of 82.60%, with Claude Opus 4.7 following closely at 82.00%

claim: SWE-bench Multimodal contains 619 task instances from 17 user-facing JavaScript repositories (web UI, data visualization, mapping), testing whether coding agents generalize to visual software domains.
quote: SWE-bench Multimodal ... 619 task instances ... 17 ... JavaScript ... repositories

claim: Systems perform far worse on SWE-bench Multimodal than on text-only SWE-bench, with top resolve rates historically in the low double digits (~12%), reflecting a large penalty when visual inputs are involved.

claim: The CodeReviewer dataset (Microsoft, EMNLP/FSE 2022) is a large multilingual corpus across nine languages used to benchmark three code-review tasks: code change quality estimation, review comment generation, and code refinement.

claim: The CodeReviewer dataset comprises roughly 150,406 training, 13,103 validation and 13,104 test examples drawn from top-starred GitHub repositories across nine popular languages.
quote: CodeReviewer ... real-world code changes and code reviews from open-source projects in nine of the most popular programming languages

claim: CRScore (NAACL 2025) is a reference-free metric grounding evaluation of code-review comments in LLM/static-analyzer-detected claims and code smells, scoring conciseness, comprehensiveness and relevance.
quote: CRScore: Grounding Automated Evaluation of Code Review Comments in Code Claims and Smells

claim: CRScore achieves the best alignment with human judgment among open-source metrics (0.54 Spearman) and ships a corpus of ~2.9k human-annotated review-quality scores for machine-generated and GitHub review comments.
quote: greatest alignment with human judgment among open source metrics (0.54 Spearman correlation) ... corpus of 2.9k human-annotated review quality scores

claim: CodeReviewQA (MSR 2025) is a comprehension benchmark of 900 manually curated instances across 9 languages that decomposes code refinement into three reasoning stages: Change Type Recognition, Change Localisation, and Solution Identification, to expose model weaknesses and reduce contamination.
quote: Change Type Recognition (CTR) ... Change Localisation (CL) ... Solution Identification (SI) ... 900 manually curated, high-quality examples ... 9 languages

claim: Martian's open-source Code Review Bench evaluates AI code-review agents using both an offline benchmark (identical PRs with known issues) and an online benchmark that measures whether developers accept or reject AI review comments in real repositories.
quote: Code Review Bench - Code Review Benchmark | Martian

claim: Martian's Code Review Bench is derived from over 200,000 pull requests (drawing on 1.2M+ real code changes from GitHub PRs involving AI bots), is updated daily, and open-sources the dataset, judge prompts, and pipeline; Martian sells no coding assistant, claiming independence.
quote: largest benchmark ... derived from more than 200,000 pull requests and updated daily ... Over 1.2 million real code changes

claim: Qodo claims #1 on Martian's benchmark with its Extended (Research Preview) config at F1 64.3% (precision 62.3%, recall 66.4%), while its Standard production version scores F1 47.9% (#4).
quote: F1 Score: 64.3% Precision: 62.3% Recall: 66.4% ... Qodo Standard ... F1 Score: 47.9% ... #4

claim: CodeRabbit separately claims #1 on Martian's online benchmark over ~300,000 PRs (Jan-Feb 2026) with F1 51.2%, precision 49.2%, recall 53.5%, illustrating that vendors cite different configs/time windows for their top-ranked claims.
quote: highest F1 score 51.2% ... Precision 49.2% ... Recall 53.5% ... nearly 300,000 pull requests

claim: RepoBench (ICLR 2024) benchmarks repository-level code auto-completion in Python and Java via three tasks (RepoBench-R retrieval, RepoBench-C completion, RepoBench-P pipeline), each with up to ~12,000 evaluation samples across multiple context-length levels.
quote: RepoBench: Benchmarking Repository-Level Code Auto-Completion Systems

claim: Martian Code Review Bench (2026) evaluated 17 AI code review tools across 200,000+ real pull requests, defining precision as the share of review comments that lead to an actual code change and recall as the share of real issues caught; top tools clustered around ~50% precision and ~50% recall.
quote: Precision: the percentage of a tool's review comments that lead to an actual code change... Recall: the percentage of real issues in a PR that the tool actually catches... F1 Score: 51.7%, Precision: 52.2%, Recall: 51.1%

claim: A two-phase field study at WirelessCar (7 interview + 10 experiment participants) found developers warn that noisy or low-priority AI review comments cause reviewers to stop reading and miss real issues, a key trust failure mode.
quote: The problem with those kinds of checks is that, if they're not good enough, you stop reading them... you miss the real issues because you start ignoring the feedback

claim: Evaluating GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash on 492 AI-generated code blocks, correctness accuracy was only 68.5% (GPT-4o) / 63.9% (Gemini) and dropped up to 22.87% without problem descriptions, leading authors to conclude LLMs are unreliable for fully automated review and recommend human-in-the-loop.
quote: LLMs would be unreliable in a fully automated code review environment... Correctness Accuracy 68.50% (GPT-4o) 63.89% (Gemini)... differences up to 22.87% observed in correction and regression ratios

claim: In an industrial study at Tencent, the static analysis tool's baseline false-positive rate was ~76% (>90% before filtering), and the best LLM method (LLM4PFA) eliminated 94-98% of false positives at 0.93-0.94 accuracy on 433 alarms.
quote: LLM4PFA...eliminates 94-98% of false positives across different backbone LLMs... false positive rate 76% in the final dataset, with the actual rate higher than 90%... 433 total alarms (328 false positives, 105 true positives)

claim: A study of 6 LLMs across 17 CVEs in 10 real-world projects found that 'bug-free' framing systematically degrades vulnerability detection (confirmation bias), and an iterative refinement attack exploiting this bias achieves a 100% success rate.
quote: 6 LLMs under five framing conditions... 17 CVEs across 10 real-world projects... iterative refinement attack...achieves 100% success... bug-free framing producing the strongest effect

claim: A case study of 16 GitHub Actions AI reviewers across 178 mature repos (22,326 AI comments) found only 0.9-19.2% of valid AI comments led to code changes versus ~60% for human comments, with hunk-level and manually-triggered tools (12.8% vs 6.8%) faring better.
quote: 0.9%-19.2% for valid AI-generated comments depending on the tool... 60% of valid human review comments led to code changes... 12.8% addressing rate for manually triggered comments versus 6.8% for automatically triggered ones

claim: Analyzing 278,790 review conversations across 300 OSS projects, AI agent comments were ~7x more verbose than humans (29.6 vs 4.1 tokens/line), concentrated >95% on code-improvement/defect-detection, and had a 16.6% adoption rate versus 56.5% for humans.
quote: 29.6 tokens per line of code... 4.1 tokens per line of code... Code Improvement and Defect Detection include over 95% of AI agent comments... Human reviewers: 56.5%... AI agents: 16.6%

claim: Hallucinations in LLM code review include fabricated package recommendations ('slopsquatting': 19.7% of 576,000 sampled packages were non-existent, 58% repeated across queries), enabling supply-chain attacks; standard AI code review carries reported 5-15% false-positive rates.
quote: 19.7% of recommended packages (205,000 total) were fabricated and non-existent... 58% of hallucinated packages repeated across multiple queries... standard AI code review generating 5-15% false positive rates

claim: CodeBERT (2020) was the first bimodal pre-trained Transformer for code+natural language, trained on NL-PL pairs in 6 languages and reaching SOTA on code search and documentation generation, establishing the encoder-model foundation for code understanding.
quote: CodeBERT, a bimodal pre-trained model for programming language (PL) and natural language (NL)... results show that CodeBERT achieves state-of-the-art performance on both natural language code search and code documentation generation tasks.

claim: CodeT5 (Sept 2021, EMNLP, Salesforce) introduced an identifier-aware encoder-decoder pre-trained on 8.35M functions in 8 languages, moving the field from encoder-only understanding to unified seq2seq generation and providing the backbone later reused by CodeReviewer.
quote: CodeT5 is a unified encoder-decoder model... proposes a novel identifier-aware pre-training task... pre-trained on 8.35M functions in 8 programming languages (Python, Java, JavaScript, PHP, Ruby, Go, C, and C#).

claim: DeepSeek-Coder (Jan 2024) shipped permissively-licensed open models 1.3B-33B trained on 2T tokens; the 33B base beat CodeLlama-34B by 7.9-10.8 points on HumanEval/MBPP and surpassed closed Codex and GPT-3.5, signalling open-weight code LLMs reaching parity.
quote: DeepSeek-Coder... surpasses existing closed-source models like Codex and GPT-3.5... compared with CodeLlama-34B, DeepSeek-Coder-Base-33B leads by 7.9%, 9.3%, 10.8% and 5.9% respectively on HumanEval Python, HumanEval Multilingual, MBPP and DS-1000.

claim: StarCoder2 (Feb 2024, BigCode) was trained on The Stack v2 (4x larger, built with Software Heritage and including GitHub PRs) at 3B/7B/15B scale, with the 3B model outperforming similar-size code LLMs and the original 15B StarCoderBase.
quote: StarCoder2 models were trained with 3B, 7B, and 15B parameters on 3.3 to 4.3 trillion tokens... StarCoder2-3B outperforms other Code LLMs of similar size on most benchmarks, and also outperforms StarCoderBase-15B.

claim: Qwen2.5-Coder (Sept 2024) released six sizes (0.5B-32B); the 7B variant beat the previous best dense DeepSeek-Coder-33B across all five metrics and the series set SOTA among same-size open models on HumanEval/MBPP, making small self-hostable models viable for review.
quote: Qwen2.5-Coder have achieved state-of-the-art results among open-source models of the same size... with Qwen2.5-Coder-7B outperforming the previous best dense model, DS-Coder-33B, across all five metrics.

claim: DeepSeek-Coder-V2 (June 2024) was an open MoE code model framed as breaking the closed-source barrier in code intelligence, evaluated on LiveCodeBench and pushing open weights toward frontier coding capability used in self-hosted review.
quote: DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence

claim: An early-2026 large-scale study of 128,018 GitHub projects estimated coding-agent adoption at 22.20-28.66% in the first half of 2025 (naming Cursor, Claude Code, Codex), evidence of the rapid agentic surge that extended into open-source PR review.
quote: an estimated adoption rate of 22.20%-28.66% among the 128,018 GitHub projects analyzed... coding agents have emerged as a category of development tools that have very quickly transitioned to the practice.

claim: By 2026 open-weight MoE models such as DeepSeek V4 advertise ~81% SWE-bench at ~$0.30/MTok, with DeepSeek V3 (late 2024) credited for proving an open-weights lab could match OpenAI/Anthropic on reasoning while releasing weights free.
quote: DeepSeek V3 launched in late 2024, proving that a Chinese AI lab could compete head-to-head with OpenAI and Anthropic on reasoning benchmarks while releasing weights for free.
